newsitem.title: USA: NYC voters see crime, schools as top concerns-poll.
newsitem.headline: NYC voters see crime, schools as top concerns-poll.

text.p: New York City voters listed crime and schools as their top concerns, a new survey said on Monday, adding those surveyed overwhelmingly approved of how Mayor Rudolph Giuliani handled the former.
But Giuliani failed to get the same high rating for education.

"Mayor Giuliani's position on crime is unassailable -- he gets an 82 percent to 15 percent approval on this issue. Education, however, is also a big concern for New York voters and the mayor could do a little homework to bring up his 48 percent to 44 percent approval on this issue," said Maurice Carroll, director of the Quinnipiac College Polling Institute, in prepared remarks.

A total of 30 percent of the 901 New York City residents who said they were registered voters identified crime or violence as the top issue mayoral candidates should address, while education was put forward by 29 percent, Quinnipiac College Polling Institute said.

Only 12 percent of those surveyed said they were satisfied with the quality of public schools, though they were evenly split when it came to rating their own neighborhood schools, with 41 percent satisfied and 40 percent unsatisfied.

While a recently established all-girls public school was supported by a wide margin -- 75 percent to 18 percent -- 55 percent of the parents wanted their children to attend a coeducational school. Yet those surveyed also would support an all-boys school by the same big amount -- 71 percent to 24 percent.

New York City Chancellor of Education, Rudy Crew, got favorable marks, with 46 percent saying they had a good opinion of him. And 61 percent to 26 percent of those who responded to the poll, which was conducted from March 19 to 25 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.3 percent, said the power of local school boards should be reduced, with more authority given to the chancellor.
